Synopsis:
    Multiple international energy majors — Chevron (US), GE Vernova (US), ONGC (India), Eni (Italy), GeoPark (Colombia) — are finalising energy agreements in Venezuela imminently. The deals largely complete a six-month migration of oil contracts under an amended hydrocarbon law granting foreign operators greater flexibility on oilfield operations, crude exports and repatriation of proceeds. Chevron is pursuing expansion in the Orinoco Belt and a diluent-supply position in Monagas North. This follows a separate large-scale US-Venezuela deal covering 17 oilfields with ~64 bn barrels of proved reserves. The focus is overwhelmingly on oil, with GE Vernova's involvement suggesting some electricity/energy infrastructure dimension.
